entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. At the instance of the opposite party no.2, the  F.I.R., i.e., Bhawanipatna Town P.S. Case No.258 of  2022 came to be registered against the petitioner  under Sections 417/420/376/294/506 of the IPC,
 pending in the Court of learned S.D.J.M.,
 Bhawanipatna.

3. The prosecution case is that the opposite party  no.2/informant lodged a written report before the  Bhawanipatna Town Police Station alleging therein  that in the month of December, 2021, the petitioner  committed forcible sex act with her by falsely  promising her to marriage.
She became pregnant.

When the informant asked the accused to marry, he  Page 1 of 4  threatened her with dire consequences and abused her in filthy languages even the petitioner also threatened the informant not to lodge any case against him.
Basing upon such information, the F.I.R. has been registered.

4. After investigation, Charge Sheet has been filed on 21.08.2022 for the alleged commission of offences punishable under Sections 417/ 420/ 376(2)(n)/ 294/
506/313/511 of the IPC against the petitioner.
During investigation, the statement of the victim has been recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. on 23.06.2022.
When the matter stood thus, the parties have settled their dispute.

Therefore, the petitioner has filed the present petition for quashing of the entire Bimal Kumar Bidyadhar vs State Of Odisha & Another .... Opp. ... on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82365111/
1

sentences.text: criminal prosecution on the ground of settlement.

5. The petitioner and opposite party no.2 have appeared before this Court in person being identified by their respective counsel and have filed their self- attested xerox copies of Aadhaar Card to establish their identity, which are taken on record.

6. The petitioner and opposite party no.2 have filed a joint affidavit dated 12.12.2024, inter alia,
stating as under:
"2. That the petitioner and Opp. party No. 2 tied the knot in the Manikeswar Temple of Bhawanipatna on 14.12.2019 as per Hindu rites and customs in presence of relatives and friends and out of wed lock a male child was born on 23.8.2022 at DI-1H Medical , Bhawanipatna.
3.

That due to some misunderstanding between the petitioner and Opp. Party No. 2 filed FIR. which was registered as Bhawanipatna Town P.S. Case No. 258 of 2022 for commission of offences U/5 417, 420, 376 (2n), 294,294 506, 313 and Section 511 of I.P.C.
4.

entities.text: Bhawanipatna Town P.S. Case No. 258 of 2022
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: That during pendency of this case the matter has been amicably settled between us at our family members in presence of the village gentries and well wishers.

5. That since the dispute between us have already settled amicably and we are living peacefully and maintaining our relationship as husband and wife and carrying our child, in this situation if the Criminal proceeding is continued it will effect the good relationship between us for which we declare the drop the proceeding to develop their cordial relationship and maintain the peacefully living of our rest of life."
7. On the query from the Court, the opposite party no.2, who is present in Court today, has stated that he has already settled the dispute with the petitioner.
Therefore, she does not want to proceed against the petitioner any more.
Hence, she joins the petitioner praying for quashing of the criminal case.
8. Mr. Jena, learned counsel for the State submits that since the parties have already settled their dispute, this Court may give indulgence, as there is no legal impediment.

9. Regard being had to the nature of offences and the fact that the parties have already settled their dispute, the present case is squarely covered by the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another, reported in 2012 (10) SCC 303, B.S. Joshi &
others vs. State of Haryana & another, reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675 and Madhavraoji Wajirao Scindia and another Vrs. Sambajirao Chandrojirao Angre and others, reported in AIR 1988 SC.
Therefore, subjecting the petitioner to the rigors of trial will be a futile exercise.
